newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton market closed for Good Friday.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton market closed for Good Friday.

text.p: The Bombay cotton market was closed on account of Good Friday. Trading resumes on Saturday.
On Thursday, Gujarat cotton rose but Punjab varieties remained steady in a narrow price band.
In spot, Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) gained 300 rupees to 13,000/13,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) and Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) rose 400/500 rupees to 19,000/20,000 rupees per candy.
Punjab saw-ginned was unchanged at 1,500/1,650 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab F-414 was quiet at 1,880/1,900 rupees and Bengal-deshi at 870/920 rupees per maund.
